rows.speaker: Said b. Mesrûk
rows.claim: Quraysh asked Jews and Christians about Moses’ and Jesus’ signs, then asked Muhammad to turn Ṣafā into gold; God warned of punishment if they denied it, but Muhammad asked to continue calling them gradually, so this verse pointed to creation as a greater sign.
rows.anchor: Said b. Mesrûk hazretlerinden rivayet olunduğuna göre, Kureyş “Yahudîlere Mûsâ’nın getirdiği âyâtı bize söyleyin nelerdi?” diye sormuşlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordered creation and its ongoing processes are greater, more beneficial, and more compelling miracles than Quraysh’s requested golden Ṣafā.
rows.anchor: semâvât u arzın halkı ve buna müteferri‘cereyân-ı hilkatin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens comprise countless celestial bodies, vast distances, visible and unseen matter or subtle qualities, paths, orbits, systems, and constellations.
rows.anchor: sayısız ecrâm-ı ulviyesi ve aralarındaki eb‘âd ve bu eb‘âdı işgal eden hevâ ve ziyâ gibi mer’î veya gayr-i mer’î ecsâm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth’s seas, lands, mountains, valleys, plains, deserts, springs, rivers, minerals, plants, and forests are linked to the heavens without pillars or girders.
rows.anchor: denizleriyle karalarıyla, dağlarıyla dereleriyle, ovalarıyla çölleriyle, pınarlarıyla ırmaklarıyla, ma‘âdiniyle nebâtâtıyla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day alternate in succession, lengthen and shorten, and manifest spatial arrangement, time, and opposites recurring in one place.
rows.anchor: gece ile gündüzün değişmesinde, uzayıp kısalmasında, birbiri ardı sıra te‘âkub etmesinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships carry useful cargo across the sea; their motion recalls celestial travel, while the created sea and laws of motion and rest provide human benefits.
rows.anchor: gemilerin cereyânında ve cereyan ettiği denizlerin sırr-ı hilkatinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water sent down from above revives dry earth after its death, displaying how plant life is formed.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın yukarıdan indirdiği suda, indirip de kuru toprağa ölümünden sonra su ile tekrar hayat vermesinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God classifies and spreads every kind, class, and species of animal across the earth, extending as far as rational beings.
rows.anchor: zevi’l-‘ukūle varıncaya kadar her türlü hayvânâtı sınıf sınıf, cins cins

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changing winds, moved from direction to direction and state to state, are another sign.
rows.anchor: türlü türlü rüzgârları bir taraftan bir tarafa, bir hâlden diğer hâle evirip çevirmesinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds subdued between heaven and earth, along with the other phenomena, are signs and material, spiritual, religious, and worldly blessings more miraculous than the requested sign.
rows.anchor: semâ ile arz arasında musahhar olan bulutlarda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs benefit people who reason and actually use their intellect; intellect itself is one of the signs and perhaps the greatest.
rows.anchor: akıllı olan ve aklından istifade eden kimseler için. Binâen‘aleyh akıl da bu âyâtın biri ve belki en büyüğüdür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intellect is an immaterial light rooted in heart and soul and radiating in the brain, by which people apprehend what is not sensed.
rows.anchor: Ma‘deni kalb ve rûhda, şu‘â‘ı dimağda bulunan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reasoning apprehends causal relations between causes and effects, agents and acts, and their necessary connections, then infers from effect to cause, cause to effect, or one effect to another.
rows.anchor: esbâb ile müsebbebât, eser ile müessir arasındaki alâkayı, yani illiyet kanununu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inference can discover an unseen animal from a rustle, honey from a bee, or honey and its location from the buzz of an unseen bee.
rows.anchor: meselâ görülen bir bal arısından gayr-i mahsüs olan bal

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Particular-to-particular inference is analogy, also called legal analogy.
rows.anchor: cüz’îden cüz’îye, ferdden ferde intikaldir ki buna “temsîl” veya “kıyâs-ı fıkhî” denilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Induction moves from particulars to universals; most or all general propositions and scientific rules are discovered this way, making observation and experiment important.
rows.anchor: vâhid-i ferdîden vâhid-i nev‘îye veya vâhid-i nev‘îden vâhid-i cinsîye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deduction moves from universal to particular and applies the sciences in practice; it derives practical results from induction and is the strongest scientific method because it both establishes and confirms.
rows.anchor: küllîden cüz’îye, vâhid-i cinsîden vâhid-i nev‘îye veya vâhid-i nev’îden vâhid-i ferdîye intikaldir ki buna da ma‘nâ-yı ehassıyla “istintac”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By apprehending and applying causality through these routes, reason necessarily recognizes God’s existence, unity, and encompassing mercy from the signs.
rows.anchor: illiyet kanununu hüsn-i idrak ve tatbik sayesinde akıl, bu âyetlerden bu tarîklerle vücud ve vahdâniyet-i ilâhiyeyi ve rahmet-i şâmilesini bi’z-zarûre anlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflective thought is reason’s slow, gradual, temporal course; intuition reaches its object immediately in a single swift leap.
rows.anchor: Birincisi ağır, tedrîcî ve zamânî olan teemmülî seyridir ki buna “fikir” tesmiye olunur. Diğeri de bir lahzada

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One kind of intuition is acquired through prolonged study, experience, and practice; theoretical and practical training cultivate it, and it is also called acquired or received intellect.
rows.anchor: tahsil, tecribe ve mümâreseden mütehassıl meleke-i i‘tiyaddır ki kesbîdir. Nazarî amelî tahsil ve terbiye-i ilmiye bu gayeye ermek içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other kind is an innate divine gift, called sacred, natural, or inborn intellect; effort does not produce it, and everyone has some share.
rows.anchor: doğrudan doğru fıtratta merkuz ve sırf vehb-i ilâhî olan melekedir ki buna da “kuvve-i kudsiyye” veya “akl-ı matbû‘”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without innate intellect, acquired intellect has no effect; innate intuition has unbounded ranks, from simple intelligence up to prophetic intellects.
rows.anchor: Bu olmayınca öbür akl-ı mesmû‘un hiç hükmü olmaz. Bunun kābil-i tahdid olmayan birçok merâtibi vardır ki bir zekâ-yı basîtten ‘ukūl-i enbiyâ mertebelerine kadar gider

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest rank, the First Intellect, sees beginning from end and end from beginning with perfect certainty and is identified as the Divine Pen and Muhammadan Light.
rows.anchor: mebde’den gāyeyi, gāyeden mebde’i

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadith reports cited here say that the first thing God created was the Prophet’s light, the Pen, or the intellect.
rows.anchor: أَوَّلُ مَا خَلَقَ اللّٰهُّٰ الْقَلَمَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Differences in intellect’s degrees arise from deficiencies; fundamentally the path of intellect is one, the path of truth.
rows.anchor: ‘Ukūlün derecâtındaki ihtilâf noksanlarından münba‘istir. Yoksa esas itibariyle ‘ukūl için tarîk birdir, o da tarîk-ı haktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innate apprehension of first principles such as causality and noncontradiction is a share in the First Intellect’s grasp and evidence of the perfection of absolute sacred power.
rows.anchor: illiyet mebde’i, tenakuz mebde’i gibi idrâk-i hakka vesile olan esbâb-ı asliye hakkındaki idrâkât-ı bedîhiyemiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings’ partial, relative intuition connects them to the First Intellect and thereby gives them access to truth.
rows.anchor: Bizim nisbî ve cüz’î olan kuvve-i hadsiyemizle Akl-ı Evvel’e böyle bir ittisâlimiz ve bu sayede hakka bir vusûlümüz vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innate intuition is not acquired by human effort, but each person’s share and the habitual intuitive skill gained through sustained experience are acquired.
rows.anchor: hads-i vehbî, kesbî olmadığı için bunda sa‘y ü irâde-i beşer âmil değil ise de, bunda bi-lutfihi teâlâ mâlik olduğumuz hissemiz nisbetinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God summons all people to reason along this path; miracles that act directly on the senses have little benefit without reason.
rows.anchor: umum insanları bu tarîka hidâyet ve sevk için لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَعْقِلُونَ buyurmuş ve akıl olmayınca doğrudan doğru hislerde icrâ-yı te’sîr edecek olan mu‘cizâtın büyük bir fâidesi olmayacağını

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an guides people toward universal rational truths more than miracles and is itself the greatest miracle.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın bu gibi âyetlerinde insanları idrak ve istidlâl için mu‘cizâttan ziyade ma‘kūlât-ı külliyeye sevk vardır. Ve bunun için Kur’an, a‘zam-ı mu‘cizâttır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This emphasis on reason must not be construed as denying prophetic miracles or claiming the Seal of the Prophets showed no physical miracles.
rows.anchor: mu‘cizât-ı enbiyânın imtinâ‘ına ve Hâtemü’l-Enbiyâ Efendimiz’in maddî mucizeler göstermediğine ve göstermeyeceğine işaret gibi bir mâna çıkarmaya kalkışmak da doğru değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the immense ongoing wonders of creation, turning Ṣafā to gold is neither significant nor impossible for divine power.
rows.anchor: Safâ tepesinin altına kalb edilivermesi bu kudrete nazaran hiçbir ehemmiyeti hâiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its revelation context, the verse says an isolated, temporary wonder is a small request beside the immense, enduring miracles of creation and the benefits of contemplating them.
rows.anchor: Safâ’nın altına kalb edilmesi gibi muvakkat ve münferid bir hâdise-i hârika talebi pek küçük bir şeydir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who study creation and follow its laws could eventually pave Ṣafā or even all Meccan mountains with gold by understanding mineral laws; they should seek greater, lasting, sacred aims.
rows.anchor: Yalnız me‘âdin kanunlarını iyice idrak etmek bu matlaba kâfî gelir. Binâberîn Allah’tan ve Peygamber’den daha büyük

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here signs means clear marks, decisive proofs, and manifest miracles that leave no serious room for objection; Qur’anic verses are called signs in this sense.
rows.anchor: âyât, alâmât-ı vâzıha ve delâil-i kat‘iyye karşısında ciddî olarak hiçbir söz söylenmek ihtimâli bulunmayan mu‘cize-i bâhire demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has active signs in the book of creation and verbal signs in the revealed book; both indicate the divine essence, attributes, rulings, and will.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın iki nevi âyâtı vardır. Birisi kitâb-ı tekvin ve hilkatteki âyât-ı fi‘liyye, diğeri de kitâb-ı münzeldeki âyât-ı kavliyyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two books and kinds of signs mutually indicate, interpret, and explain one another.
rows.anchor: ve bu iki nevi âyâtı mütekābilen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perfect knowledge reads creation’s active signs through the revealed book, then recognizes God’s essence and attributes and follows divine laws toward the straight path and abiding in God.
rows.anchor: kitâb-ı münzelin âyât-ı kavliyyesinden kitâb-ı hilkatin âyât-ı fi‘liyyesini ve ondan Hak teâlâ’nın zât u sıfâtını okuyup anlamak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise verse gathers clear evidence that one sustaining Creator orders the varied universe, possesses encompassing power and mercy, suffices for all beings, and has no peer; both ordinary and high intellects can grasp it.
rows.anchor: Kayyûm-ı kül olan vücûd-i vâhidini izhar eyleyen Hak teâlâ’nın Zât-ı ehadiyyetine ve kudret ve rahmet-i şâmilesine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an takes the roots of the highest scientific aims and makes them clear and simple enough for people of every capacity to understand.
rows.anchor: Kur’an en yüksek metâlib-i ulûm ve fünûnun bu vechile cezrini alarak bütün havâss u avâmmın vuzuh ile anlayacağı derecede basitlendirip tâlim ediverir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People habituated to empty, transient poetic fantasy may fail to feel the Qur’an’s miraculous height because their natural taste and reason have been impoverished by caprice.
rows.anchor: zevk-i fıtrîlerinin ve akıllarının hevâiyyât içinde iflas etmiş olmasında aramalıdırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sexual relations with one’s wife are lawful at any hour of the fasting night; the earlier restriction after the evening prayer or sleep no longer applies.
rows.anchor: Gecenin hangi saatinde olursa olsun herkes halîlesine mu‘âmele-i zevciye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The former rule inferred from the earlier communities’ fasting and the previous rule taken from Prophetic practice were abrogated; Ramadan fasting abrogated the earlier fasts, showing that Scripture may abrogate Sunnah.
rows.anchor: şerâyi‘-i sâlife hükmü, kezâlik savm-ı evvelde sünnet-i nebeviyeden me’huz olan hükm-i sâbık ba‘demâ mensuhtur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafath is obscene explicit speech about what should be stated indirectly, and by metonymy may mean intercourse; here it unanimously means physical intercourse, not verbal obscenity.
rows.anchor: “Refes”, fuhş-i kelâm yani kinayesi îcab eden şeyi açık söylemektir ki kinaye olarak cimâ‘a da ıtlak olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wills ease for this community: He shortened the fasting period, removed the night restriction, and made sexual relations lawful at night.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah ümmet-i Muhammed’e yüsr murad ettiğinden, savmın vaktini kısaltmış, geceleri nesh etmiş, refesi helâl kılmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spouses are garments for one another: they embrace and cover each other, conceal faults, protect from heat and cold, guard chastity, and protect one another from fornication.
rows.anchor: diğer cihetten elbisenin ayıpları örtmesi, soğuk ve sıcaktan koruması gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew that believers were betraying themselves by failing to restrain themselves and exposing themselves to loss of reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: sabredemiyor, nefislerinizi tenkīs-i sevâba ve teveccüh-i ‘ikāba mâruz kılarak kendinize zulm ediyordunuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted their repentance and erased the sin of sexual relations during the fasting night.
rows.anchor: Allah size atf-ı nazar etti, tevbenizi kabul

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Seek what God wrote for you” may mean seeking the offspring eternally decreed for you in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın sizin için ezelde yazdığı, takdir ettiği, Levh-i Mahfûz’a nakş eylediği zürriyeti talep edin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation of “seek what God wrote for you” is to seek the lawful place of intercourse.
rows.anchor: Diğer bir mâna ile: Allah’ın meşrû kıldığı mevzi‘-i tenâsülü talep edin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation of “seek what God wrote for you” is to seek the Night of Decree.
rows.anchor: Üçüncü bir mâna ile: Kadir gecesini arayın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mubashara literally denotes skin touching skin and is conventionally used for intercourse; intercourse is unanimously the intended meaning here.
rows.anchor: çıplak deri deriye dokunmaktır. Bu münâsebetle cimâ‘a da ıtlak olunur ki, burada murad bu olduğu müttefekun ‘aleyhtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to have relations, like the command to eat and drink, grants permission rather than imposing an obligation.
rows.anchor: İşbu بَٰشِرُوهُنَّ emrinin وَكُلُوا۟ gibi ibâha için olduğu da müttefekun ‘aleyhtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following command to seek what God decreed indicates that the aim of intercourse should be offspring rather than mere gratification, since lawful sex and desire serve procreation and the continuation of the species.
rows.anchor: mübâşeretten maksad evlâd olmalı, mücerred kazâ-yı şehvet tâkip edilmemelidir. Zira halk-ı şehvetin ve meşrû‘iyyet-i nikâhın hikmeti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret “seek what God wrote” as prohibiting coitus interruptus, but the text does not make this certain because its object is unstated; hadith nevertheless suggest disapproval.
rows.anchor: Bu وَٱبْتَغُوا۟ emrinin azilden nehy olduğu da söylenmiş ise de mef‘ûl-i ibtiğā olan ما sarih olmadığından kat‘î değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating and drinking remain permitted until the white thread of true dawn becomes distinct from the black thread; this is the first light of dawn.
rows.anchor: Fecirden olan, fecr-i sâdıktan bir cüz bulunan beyaz iplik. Yani sabahleyin şafak sökünceye, tan yeri iplik gibi ağarıncaya kadar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “until” excludes its endpoint, so fasting must already begin when the white thread becomes distinct; if uncertain, refraining is recommended, but eating does not require a make-up fast because distinction means certain knowledge.
rows.anchor: hayt-ı ebyaz tebeyyün ettiği zaman imsak da başlamış bulunmak farzdır. Meşkuk olursa yememek müstehabdır, yenirse kazâ lâzım gelmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the clarification “from dawn” was revealed after some people used actual black and white threads to decide when to stop eating; it explains the familiar metaphor of the first dawn light and the legal day’s start.
rows.anchor: Bundan evvel bazı kimseler biri beyaz biri siyah iki iplik alır ve bunlar birbirinden seçilinceye kadar imsak yapmazlarmış, bu hâdise üzerine مِنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ beyânı nâzil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legal theory debates whether clarification came after it was needed; Elmalılı holds that delaying a clarification that changes the rule is impermissible, so on this report the verse must be abrogation rather than mere clarification.
rows.anchor: doğrusu beyân-ı tağyîrin vakt-i hâcetten te’hîri câiz değildir. Ve bu rivayete nazaran ref‘-i ihtimâl beyân-ı tağyîr değil, beyân-ı tebdîl yani nesh addolunmak lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True dawn is the true morning; false dawn is called dawn only with the qualifier “false,” and scholars unanimously place the legal day and fasting obligation at true dawn.
rows.anchor: Fecrin hakikati subh-ı sâdıktır. Subh-ı kâzibe ancak kâzib kaydıyla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says the white thread must be false dawn because its vertical column resembles a thread, whereas true dawn spreads horizontally, implying fasting should start earlier.
rows.anchor: Beyaz ipliğe benzeyen sabah beyazlığı subh-i kâzibin beyazı olmalıdır. Çünkü bu ‘amûdî ve mustatîl olduğundan ipliğe benzer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects that objection: the first true dawn is initially thin, so its horizontal spread does not prevent comparison to a thread; the forbidden amount of light is the first instant of true dawn.
rows.anchor: yemenin hurmetini gösterecek olan beyazlık mikdârı subh-ı sâdıkın evveli ve ilk lahzasıdır. Fecr-i sâdık ibtidâ münteşir olmadan evvel küçük ve ince olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra and Hasan b. Ṣāliḥ b. Cinnī held that a person who reaches dawn in a state of major ritual impurity without bathing has no valid fast.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hureyre hazretleriyle Hasan b. Sâlih b. Cinnî “cünüb olup da gusletmeden sabahı edenin orucu sahih olmayacağına” zâhib olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority holds that the fast is valid if one observes the fast on time despite remaining in major impurity at dawn, since this verse permits intercourse up to dawn and thus permits delaying the bath.
rows.anchor: cumhûr-ı ulemâya göre vaktinde imsak eden kimse cünüb de olsa orucu sahih olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At true dawn, stop eating and intercourse, then abstain completely until night; legal fasting is intentional abstention from food, drink, intercourse, and analogous bodily intake from dawn to the end of the legal day.
rows.anchor: sıyâm-ı şer‘î böyle niyetle evvel-i fecrden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This legal fast is a particular kind of lexical abstention defined by the additional limits and boundaries established by sacred law.
rows.anchor: ma‘nâ-yı lügavîsine munzam olan kuyûd ve hudûd-ı şer‘iye ile imsâk-i lügavîden bir nev‘-i mahsustur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting has three requirements: the proper time, intention, and abstention.
rows.anchor: orucun farzları üçtür: Vakit, niyet, imsaktir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fast lasts from true dawn to sunset, the legal day, rather than from sunrise to sunset as in ordinary or astronomical reckoning.
rows.anchor: vakt-i savm, tulû‘-i fecirden gurûb-i şemse kadar nehâr-ı şer‘îdir. Tulû‘-ı şemsten gurûb-ı şemse kadar olan nehâr-ı örfî veya nücûmî değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intention must be associated with most of the day, while abstention must last through the entire day; eating after dawn makes the fast invalid.
rows.anchor: Niyet de ekser-i nehâra olsun muzâf olmak lâzımdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith “Actions are only by intentions” supports intention as a general legal condition for acts of worship.
rows.anchor: kavâ‘id-i umûmiyye-i şer‘iyeden olduğu da mâlumdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No part of the night is fasting time, and every fast-breaking act is permitted throughout it.
rows.anchor: Gecenin evvelinden âhirine kadar hiçbir cüz‘ü, vakt-i savm değildir. Bunda muftırâtın hepsi mubahtır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some wrongly infer that because legal morning starts at dawn, fasting must continue after sunset until twilight or even stars; the verse begins the day “from dawn” but ends it “at night,” and night begins with eastern darkness after sunset.
rows.anchor: evvel-i nehârda مِنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ buyurulmuş, sonra itmâma إِلَى ٱلَّيْلِ ile nihâyet verilmiştir. Gurûb-ı şemsten sonra şark tarafından karanlık zuhur eder etmez de akşam olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Applying the dawn rule by analogy to twilight would alter the explicit text; the revelation context also indicates the former fast did not include the time from sunset to the evening prayer.
rows.anchor: Bunu sabaha kıyas etmek nassı tebdil eylemek demektir. Zaten sebeb-i nüzûlden anlaşıldığı üzere akşamdan yatsıya kadar zaman

rows.speaker: Acemler (Ca‘feriyye mezhebinde bulunan)
rows.claim: Persians of the Jaʿfarī school wait to see the stars before breaking the fast.
rows.anchor: Ca‘feriyye mezhebinde bulunan Acemler, yıldızı görmeden iftar etmezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexical sense of fasting as abstention also suggests restraint by all outward and inward faculties: tongue from lies, slander, and idle speech; eye from doubtful sights; ear from entertainments; soul from desires; heart from love of the world; spirit from afterlife pleasures; and inner secret from witnessing anything besides God.
rows.anchor: lisânın sıyâmı kizbden, nemîmeden, mâlâya‘nîden imsak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse can indicate these broader forms of abstinence, Elmalılı does not claim that every one is obligatory.
rows.anchor: İtmam emri bütün bunlara delâlet ederse de hepsi vücûb tarîkiyle olduğu iddia edilemez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the preceding focus on eating, drinking, and intercourse, obligatory restraint is limited to these and analogous things entering the body; other restraint is recommended virtue and fasting etiquette.
rows.anchor: bunlara mülhak olan şeylerden bedenin bâtın hükmünü hâiz olan dâhilini imsaktir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sexual relations are forbidden both day and night during mosque retreat, though otherwise lawful on fasting nights.
rows.anchor: siz mescidlerde i‘tikaf hâlinde iken ne gece, ne gündüz kadınlarınıza asla mübâşerette bulunmayınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linguistically iʿtikāf is staying confined in a place; legally it means remaining in a mosque with the intention of retreat, as the verse’s mosque qualification specifies.
rows.anchor: Lügatta “i‘tikaf” bir yerde habs-i nefs ederek durup beklemektir. Şer‘an da bir mescidde i‘tikaf niyetiyle meks etmektir

rows.speaker: İmam Muhammed
rows.claim: According to the apparent narration from Imam Muhammad, even a stay of one hour could count as legal iʿtikāf, which would mean fasting is not a condition and voluntary retreat can be done fasting or not.
rows.anchor: İmam Muhammed’in zâhir-i rivâyeti de böyledir. Bu surette i‘tikafta savm, şart olmamak lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From the verse’s context, Elmalılı infers that iʿtikāf entails fasting: the ban on intercourse particularizes the night permission, making fasting a condition and the retreat at least one day; this is proper legal iʿtikāf.
rows.anchor: i‘tikâfın sıyâmı müstelzim olduğu anlaşılır. Zira وَلَا تُبَٰشِرُوهُنَّ nehyi leyle-i sıyamdaki ibâha-i mübâşeret hükmünü muhassıs mevki‘inde olmakla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith “There is no iʿtikāf except with fasting” supports making fasting a condition.
rows.anchor: i‘tikâfta savmın şart olduğuna

rows.speaker: İmam-ı A‘zam
rows.claim: A report from Abū Ḥanīfa says iʿtikāf is valid only in a congregational mosque or, at minimum, a mosque where the five daily prayers are held; a hadith’s mention of congregational mosque means mosques in their fullest sense.
rows.anchor: İmam-ı A‘zam’dan bunun ancak mescid-i câmi‘de olabileceği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women may perform iʿtikāf only in their home prayer place; the Prophet prohibited their retreat elsewhere.
rows.anchor: Ancak kadınlar için evlerindeki mescidden başkasında i‘tikaf câiz olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A conditional or unconditional vow makes iʿtikāf obligatory; retreat during Ramadan’s last ten days is an emphasized Sunnah, and other times are recommended.
rows.anchor: İ‘tikaf, mu‘allak veya müneccez nezr ile vâcib olur. Ramazanın ‘aşr-ı ahîri içinde, yani yirmisinden sonraki günlerde sünnet-i müekkededir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two Ṣaḥīḥ collections report that the Prophet consistently observed iʿtikāf in Ramadan’s last ten days from his arrival in Medina until his death.
rows.anchor: Sahîhayn’da dahi rivayet olunduğu üzere Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz Medine’ye teşriflerinden vefâtına kadar ramazanın ‘aşr-ı ahîrinde i‘tikâfa muvâzabet buyurmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When ʿĀʾisha, Ḥafṣa, and Zaynab successively came to retreat in tents in the mosque, the Prophet stopped them, left iʿtikāf that Ramadan, and made it up in Shawwāl’s first ten days.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe ve Hazret-i Hafsa ve Hazret-i Zeyneb’in dahi müte‘âkiben gelip mescid-i sa‘âdette birer çadır kurarak i‘tikâfa girmeleri üzerine bunları nehyetmiş

rows.speaker: Zührî
rows.claim: Zuhri wondered how people could abandon iʿtikāf when the Prophet sometimes did and omitted other practices but never abandoned iʿtikāf until death.
rows.anchor: Zührî demiştir ki: “Acaba nâs i‘tikâfı nasıl terk ediyorlar?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s continued practice might suggest obligation, but companions who omitted it without rebuke show it is Sunnah rather than obligatory; his omission one Ramadan also indicates it was not individually obligatory, while making it up shows no year passed without it.
rows.anchor: ‘adem-i inkâr ile beraber muvâzabet ise delîl-i vücûb değil, delîl-i sünniyet olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without the evidence of companions’ omissions going unrebuked, the Prophet’s never missing iʿtikāf within a year would imply that at least one retreat each year was obligatory.
rows.anchor: ‘adem-i inkâr ciheti olmasa idi, hiç olmazsa senede bir i‘tikaf vâcib olurdu

rows.speaker: Katâde
rows.claim: Qatada reports that in an earlier religious law a man could leave iʿtikāf, have intercourse with his wife, and return; this verse prohibited that practice.
rows.anchor: Katâde’den menkuldür ki evvelce bir adam i‘tikâfa girerdi ve arada çıkar, zevcesine mübâşerette bulunur, yine avdet ederdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Islamic law, intercourse with women invalidates iʿtikāf; the intended meaning of “mubashara” here is intercourse.
rows.anchor: şerî‘at-ı İslâmiyede kadınlara mübâşeret i‘tikâfı müfsiddir. Ve evvelki gibi bu mübâşeretten dahi murad vat’dır

rows.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
rows.claim: One report from al-Shāfiʿī takes the second occurrence of “mubashara” more broadly as skin-to-skin contact, so even touching a woman with desire invalidates iʿtikāf.
rows.anchor: İmam Şâfiî hazretlerinden bir rivayette bu ikincisi vat’dan e‘amdır ve mülâkāt-ı beşereteyn mânasınadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mentioned rulings are either the limits God established or prohibited limits; believers must not even approach them, much less transgress them.
rows.anchor: ahkâm-ı mezkûre Allah’ın vaz‘ettiği hudûddur, yahut hudûd-ı memnû‘adır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith compares God’s prohibitions to a ruler’s protected pasture: those who graze near it risk entering it; jurists derive the principle of blocking the means from this warning.
rows.anchor: her hükümdarın bir korusu vardır. Allah’ın korusu da mehârimi, yani nehyettiği, haram kıldığı şeylerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explains the signs that guide people to His legislation clearly and eloquently so they may guard themselves by avoiding disobedience to His commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: Görüyorsunuz ya, Allah insanlara teşrî‘ettiği ahkâma delâlet edecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After completing the fasts and learning not to approach forbidden limits, believers return to the permission to eat and drink for the festival, though the passage then continues.
rows.anchor: bu sayılı günlerin oruçlarını ikmâl ü itmam ettikten ve Allah’ın hudûd-ı memnû‘asına yaklaşmamak terbiyesini aldıktan sonra siz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the protector, helper, and ruler of affairs of those whose faith was established in eternal knowledge.
rows.anchor: Allah iman edenlerin, ilm-i ezelîde imanı mukarrer olanların muhibbi ve veliyyü’l-emridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings believers from darkness into light through guidance and enabling grace.
rows.anchor: Onları hidâyet ü tevfîkiyle zulmetlerden nûra çıkarır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural “darknesses” and singular “light” are significant: many kinds of darkness exist, but one light removes them all.
rows.anchor: Burada “zulümât”ın cem‘, “nûr”un müfred getirilmesi ne kadar şâyân-ı dikkattir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one light is God’s light, as Qur’an 24:35 says; without it, human beings are overwhelmed by darkness, while its appearance restores joy and perception.
rows.anchor: Bütün bu zulmetleri izâle edecek olan nûr ise birdir ki o da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God’s light appears, sorrow and constriction lift, hearts expand, and people experience the delight of existence; this flash of delight makes one exclaim, “life, life.”
rows.anchor: işte nûr-i Hakk’ın bu bir lemha-i zevkidir ki insana “hayat hayat!” dedirtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who seek to make this joy eternal should stop leaving themselves to themselves and hold fast to God’s firm bond to attain His light.
rows.anchor: kendini kendine bırakmaktan vazgeçip nûr-i Hakk’a ermek için O’nun ‘urve-i vüskāsına yapışmalıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each matter has one true aspect through which it is approached in God, while its false aspects are innumerable; if a lost object is wrongly thought absent from its actual place, every other location is false.
rows.anchor: Mâlum ki her şeyde ancak bir vech-i Hak vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s light is knowledge, and as it appears people leave darkness; light is positive existence, darknesses are privations, and only God sustains all beings.
rows.anchor: Nûr vücûdî, bütün zulmetler ‘ademîdir. Bir vücûda nâmütenâhî ‘adem tekabül eder. Bütün mevcûdât üzerinde kayyûm olan da ancak Allah teâlâ’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith in God begins the dawn of divine light, certain knowledge, and absolute spiritual openness.
rows.anchor: Allah’a iman nûr-ı Hakk’ın, ma‘rifet-i yakīniyenin, inşirâh-ı mutlakın mebde’-i tulû‘u, fecr-i sâdıkıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despair, disbelief, doubt, misguidance, ignorance, deficient knowledge, sin, caprice, poor formation, ingratitude, immorality, and failure to recognize limits are all forms of darkness.
rows.anchor: ‘adem, yeis, küfür, reyb, vesvese, dalâl, cehil, ilm-i nâkıs, fısk, hevâ, terbiyesizlik, nankörlük, ahlâksızlık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darkness includes disbelief, sin, and doubt, and even inferential knowledge is dark relative to direct unveiling; light is corresponding knowledge and certainty, from faith-certainty to witnessed certainty.
rows.anchor: zulümât-ı küfr ü me‘âsîden, zulümât-ı şekk ü şübheden, ulûm-ı istidlâliyenin merâtib-i kaviyyesine nazaran merâtib-i za‘îfesinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God takes believers by the hand, gives them certainty, success in their affairs, discipline in their souls, openness in their hearts, and eternal happiness on the straight path.
rows.anchor: nûr-i yakīn ile işlerinde muvaffakiyet, nefislerine edeb, gönüllerine inşirah bahşeder. Tarîk-i müstakīmde sa‘âdet-i ebediyeye mazhar eyler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among unbelievers, some believe in both God and taghuts, some only in taghuts, and some in neither but rely only on themselves; the last type most often becomes taghut.
rows.anchor: Bunların bir kısmı Allah’a az çok inansa bile aynı zamanda tâgūtlara da inanırlar. Bir kısmı Allah’a inanmaz tâgūtlara inanır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taghuts are the unbelievers’ rulers of affairs; through oppression, coercion, trickery, or deception, they seize control over people.
rows.anchor: bunların evliyâ-yı umûru tâgūtlardır. Başlarına azgınlar çöker, kahr u ikrah ile veya hîle ve hud‘a ile her taraflarını kıskıvrak bağlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taghuts draw people from the innate light of faith and the straight path into darkness, because they oppose clear and upright conduct and drag people toward wrong paths.
rows.anchor: tarîk-i müstakīmden çıkarır, karanlıklara çekerler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taghuts despise reason and knowledge, corrupt thought and morals, try to rival God and the prophets through impossible projects, and recruit those who do not fear God, leading them into darkness and inextricable calamity.
rows.anchor: Akıl ve ilmi sevmez, fikirleri ihtiyarları ifsad eder, ahlâkları bozar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers together with their taghuts become people of the Fire and remain there eternally.
rows.anchor: Bunlar orada kalırlar da tâgūtlar kurtulur mu? Hayır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even those who reject both God and taghuts to rely on themselves cannot escape taghut domination; human society requires authority and rules, so rejecting divine commands leaves people subject to taghut commands.
rows.anchor: insanın cemiyetsiz, emirsiz, nehiysiz yaşaması kābil olmadığından Allah’ın teklîfini, Allah’ın emirlerini dinlemeyenler, behemehâl tâgūtların emirlerine mahkum olacaklardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coercive tyrants who reject religion cannot ultimately save themselves, and the destination of unrestrained selves that recognize no truth is hellfire.
rows.anchor: hak tanımayan kuduz nefislerin sürükleyeceği yer nâr-ı cehennemdir
